judgment.rationale: The WPF exception stack is real but identifies framework theme invalidation rather than the PowerToys element or binding that must be changed.
evidence: The report includes a PowerToys Run 0.100.2 diagnostic stack ending in PresentationFramework ThemeManager.OnSystemThemeChanged and SetupDefaultValueConverter.
The stack does not identify the failing FrameworkElement, DependencyProperty, or XAML resource.
Related issues show the same stack across releases and wake, docking, or theme changes.
Known Program plugin icon FileNotFoundException entries occur nearby but have a different stack and are not proven causal.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a fresh bug report and a focused reproduction matrix before selecting a product code fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix may apply, but the current evidence supports only a red, guarded investigation plan rather than an implementation-ready design.

proposed_fixes.title: Identify the failing WPF theme binding before changing PowerToys Run
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Provisional: a WPF style or data-trigger binding is reevaluated during system-theme resource invalidation and throws a NullReferenceException; the exact target is not known.
plan: Capture the exception immediately after reproduction with theme, high-contrast, sleep, dock, and Run visibility state recorded.
Instrument or enable binding diagnostics around ThemeManager and the Run XAML resource update path to identify the target element and property.
If the exact PowerToys binding is identified, replace the failing trigger/binding with a theme-safe property path and add a focused regression; otherwise evaluate a narrowly stack-matched mitigation.
verification: The diagnostic matrix identifies a reproducible trigger and exact binding or confirms an upstream WPF framework defect before implementation.

confidence.rationale: The stack is consistent with a theme-resource race, but several PowerToys and framework causes remain plausible.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run reports a WPF NullReferenceException during theme-resource invalidation, but the available stack is too generic to safely identify a PowerToys fix.
known_information: The affected component is PowerToys Run on Windows build 26200.0 with version 0.100.2.0.
The exception occurs on the UI thread in WPF binding and ThemeManager internals.
Related reports span several releases and mention wake, docking, and theme changes.
PowerLauncher theme and XAML trigger code are plausible ownership areas.
inferences: The issue may be a framework/system-theme invalidation race rather than a single recent PowerToys change.
Suppressing the error window without identifying the failing visual tree could hide a real UI corruption.
issue_context.analysis: A fresh trace and controlled trigger matrix are needed to distinguish a faulty PowerToys binding from a .NET/WPF servicing issue. The request is limited to evidence that changes ownership or implementation decisions.
initial_investigation: Inspected PowerLauncher ThemeManager, ErrorReporting, ExceptionHelper, App resources, LauncherControl triggers, and ResultList styles.
Reviewed related historical reports and recent theme-resource changes.
Fork mirror Issue 643 records the provisional design and adversary decision.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured immediately after the exception
information_gaps.why_needed: It may correlate the WPF exception with the triggering theme, monitor, sleep, or dock transition.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once, then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

information_gaps.information: The trigger matrix: theme toggle, high contrast, sleep/hibernate, dock/undock, Run visible versus hidden, and current versus 0.100.2 build
information_gaps.why_needed: It distinguishes a deterministic PowerToys binding path from a framework/system transition.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Record each case as a numbered result in a follow-up comment.

design.root_cause: Not established. The best current hypothesis is a WPF DataTrigger or dynamic resource binding being reevaluated during ThemeManager.OnSystemThemeChanged, but the stack does not identify the failing PowerToys element.
evidence: [Observed] The exception is NullReferenceException in PresentationFramework.SetupDefaultValueConverter during system-theme resource changes.
[Observed] PowerToys Run has custom theme dictionary and trigger paths in the candidate files.
[Observed] Similar reports span releases, weakening a single-release regression hypothesis.
[Inferred] A stack-exact reporting mitigation could be considered only after confirming the UI remains healthy.

affected_files.purpose: Applies system theme and resource updates.
Handles dispatcher exceptions and user-facing reports.
Contains result-list dynamic resource and trigger paths.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: WPF reevaluates theme resources and bindings during a system-theme message, but the failing target is not identified.
implementation_steps.change: Collect exact target-element and binding diagnostics first; only rewrite the proven binding or resource path.
implementation_steps.code_block: OnThemeChanged -> capture target FrameworkElement + DependencyProperty + resource key -> reproduce -> replace only the proven trigger/binding with a theme-safe property path.
edge_cases: Keep all resource mutation on the dispatcher thread.
Test light/dark, high contrast, monitor changes, and sleep/wake.
Do not conflate DWM composition exceptions with this WPF binding exception.
tests: Add an exact-stack ExceptionHelper test only if a mitigation is approved.
Add manual theme regression coverage for the identified XAML path.

verify: Reproduce after adding a comment containing /bugreport and record the transition that triggers the exception.
Check whether current main and the latest .NET runtime still reproduce.
If a binding is identified, build PowerLauncher with the existing tools\build\build.cmd workflow and repeat theme, high-contrast, sleep, and dock scenarios.
Ensure unrelated UI exceptions still produce the error report.
risks: A broad NullReferenceException suppression could hide broken UI state.
A speculative XAML rewrite could miss the framework defect and churn unrelated templates.
alternatives: Wait for a confirmed dotnet/WPF servicing fix if the target is framework-owned.
Use an exact-stack mitigation only with repeat-count monitoring and proof that Run remains functional.

adversary.verdict: Blocking objection remains: the failing binding and safe ownership are unknown.

comment.body: The WPF stack and related reports narrow this to theme-resource invalidation, but they do not identify the failing PowerToys control or whether the cause is framework-owned. Please reproduce once and add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward, then report whether it occurs during theme or high-contrast changes, sleep/hibernate, dock/undock, with Run visible versus hidden, and on current main. This evidence will determine whether a safe XAML fix, an exact-stack mitigation, or a framework issue is appropriate.
